lab_table.hypothesis: Mid-size inclusions are under-covered (mid-tertile recall 0.50 vs high 0.80) and 0.3-0.5 was too small while 0.3-0.7 worked; widening inclusion scale to 0.3-0.8 adds mid-size pastes (~63-72px from ~90px sources) without touching the small end. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 > 0.36 and mAP50 >= 0.61 vs control; if inclusion drops, the upper end is irrelevant and 0.3-0.7 stands.

Round 2 showed prefer_small raised inclusion AP (0.384 vs 0.352) but the mAP loss came from scratches (0.622 vs 0.712); scoping prefer_small to inclusion only should capture the inclusion gain while protecting scratches. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 >= 0.38 and scratches AP50 >= 0.69; if inclusion does not rise, source-size selection is not the lever and I keep uniform.

Several missed inclusions are clustered multi-blob defects (val images 6, 10, 15 show multiple dark spots in one region); raising inclusion max_overlap from 0.15 to 0.30 lets pastes cluster into multi-blob shapes resembling them. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 and small-tertile recall rise vs control; if inclusion drops, overlap creates unrealistic blends and I keep 0.15.

lesson: Widening inclusion scale to 0.3-0.8 was the winning final-round lever (inclusion 0.352→0.407, mAP 0.612→0.633), confirming mid-size coverage matters as much as the small end. prefer_small (even scoped to inclusion only) keeps destabilizing scratches, and high max_overlap (0.30) destroys inclusion AP — avoid both. If iterating further, the scale band is the productive knob; allocation and source-size selection are exhausted.
